Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From a- +‎ terra +‎ -izar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /a.te.ʁiˈza(ʁ)/ [a.te.hiˈza(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /a.te.ʁiˈza(ʁ)/ [a.te.hiˈza(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /a.te.ʁiˈza(ɾ)/ [a.te.hiˈza(ɾ)]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /a.te.ʁiˈza(ʁ)/ [a.te.χiˈza(χ)]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /a.te.ʁiˈza(ɻ)/ [a.te.hiˈza(ɻ)]
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ɐ.tɨ.ʁiˈzaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ɐ.tɨ.ʁiˈzaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /ɐ.tɨ.ʁiˈza.ɾi/

  • Hyphenation: a‧ter‧ri‧zar

Verb

[edit]

aterrizar (first-person singular present aterrizo, first-person singular preterite aterrizei, past participle aterrizado)

  1. (Brazil) alternative form of aterrissar

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From a- +‎ tierra (“earth”) +‎ -izar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ateriˈθaɾ/ [a.t̪e.riˈθaɾ] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • IPA(key): /ateriˈsaɾ/ [a.t̪e.riˈsaɾ] (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Rhymes: -aɾ
  • Syllabification: a‧te‧rri‧zar

Verb

[edit]

aterrizar (first-person singular present aterrizo, first-person singular preterite aterricé, past participle aterrizado)

  1. (intransitive) to land (e.g. an airplane)
    Antonym: despegar
  2. (intransitive, figuratively, colloquial) to come back to reality, to stop dreaming
